projects.name: TakeNotes
projects.cardTitle: The notebook that knows what you forget
projects.tags: Personal project · Product design · iPad app
projects.about: An iPad notebook for university students: write by hand, mark what matters, and the app turns your own marks into quizzes and a revision plan before the exam.

summary.problem: Students reread and highlight, which barely helps memory, and most only test themselves the night before an exam.
summary.role: Solo product designer: research, UX/UI, the native iPad app and its landing page. Claude wrote the code under my direction.
summary.decision: Anything you mark becomes a question that comes back before you forget it. A dedicated marker always makes a question, because pen gestures worked about 1 time in 4 at lecture speed.
summary.unvalidated: Whether it improves retention. Beta feedback (13 TestFlight testers) is informal: no counts, no recordings.

projects.name: DeciBuy
projects.tags: Independent concept · Product design · Research & prototyping
projects.about: A phone app that looks at a price, your spare money and your payday, and answers before you pay: Buy, Wait for payday or Not now.

summary.problem: People buy in minutes, often late at night, and the regret comes later. Few do the “can I afford it” math before every purchase.
summary.role: Solo product designer: research, UX, UI and a coded prototype, with Claude as a production and critique partner.
summary.decision: Three equal answers, Buy, Wait for payday or Not now, from ranges asked once. No spending log, no bank connection.
summary.unvalidated: Almost everything: most research was AI-simulated, so every decision is a hypothesis until tested with real people. Not launched.

projects.name: Leeway
projects.tags: John Bryce capstone · UX/UI · Research & usability testing
projects.about: Pre-book a time slot for the security check at Ben Gurion Airport, and get guided until check-in is done. Research, a 12-screen app and a live prototype.

summary.problem: The security interview at Ben Gurion is unpredictable, so travelers arrive about three hours early just in case (3 of 4 interviewees).
summary.role: Solo, John Bryce capstone: research, UX/UI, design system and a 12-screen front-end prototype in 4 languages.
summary.decision: Book only the security screening. Check-in is shown, never promised: a check-in slot would be a guess dressed as a reservation.
summary.unvalidated: Usability: up to seven people tried it informally, with no tasks or recordings. Real capacity needs airport integration.
